name: Gula (Chad)
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Only Bombay 2010 3-page wordlist per Glottolog; no grammar or phonology exists.

sources.citation: SIL Global archive landing page for Bombay 2010,https://www.sil.org/resources/archives/9040;and the held SIL OAI-PMH dump searched for glu / Gula (Chad) / Bayo
sources.note: SIL's own catalogue holds nothing else for Bayo/Gula (Chad): the only Chad record matching is Bombay 2010 (oai:sil.org:267161, 38 pages, 'language surveys').

sources.citation: Glottolog hh.bib (Hammarström's bibliography, copy consulted) and Glottolog CLDF 5.1 sources.bib: all entries tagged [glu] or mentioning Gula/Nougayrol
sources.note: Only Bombay 2010 carries language code [glu]. Nougayrol 1999 'Les Parlers Gula: Centrafrique, Soudan, Tchad' (CNRS, 382 pp., listed by Glottolog as a grammar) is coded 'Gula of Vakaga in CAR (Mere-Sara Gula-Malu-Zura-Koto de Kurbu) = Gula [kcm]'. Dalmais 1961 'Goula Mamoun' = [kcm]. No other Gula (Chad) item exists in the bibliography.

sources.citation: Keegan, John M. Sara-Bagirmi Languages Project (Morkeg Books), Bagirmi languages page,https://morkegbooks.com/Services/World/Languages/SaraBagirmi/;Keegan's Sara-Bagirmi Bibliography (held)
sources.note: Gula [glu] is listed among the Bagirmi languages with Ethnologue demographics only ('some 10,000 speakers.. southwest of Lake Iro'); no dictionary, grammar or phonology offered; the bibliography has no Gula (Chad)/Bayo entry.

sources.citation: Wikipedia en 'Gula language (Chad)' and fr 'Goula (langue)'; ISO 639-3 record glu (iso639-3.sil.org/code/glu); Chan, Numeral Systems of the World's Languages index (https://lingweb.eva.mpg.de/channumerals/)
sources.note: en-Wikipedia: stub citing Ethnologue only. fr-Wikipedia 'Goula' describes the CAR Gula (kara/Vakaga; 3-4 tone registers per Nougayrol 1999), not glu. ISO record gives only the reference name. Chan's index has no Gula (Chad)/Bayo entry.

Nothing on phonology. Identity data only: alt names Goula, Sara Gula; location Moyen-Chari region, Lac Iro department, Alako and Boum-Kebir subprefectures, southwest of Lake Iro, and Guéra border area; dialects Kofoy, Malé, Moufa, Souka, Toussa; 'Probably related to Disa [dsi]'; 'Different from Gula Iro [glj] of Chad, which is Adamawa, and from Gula [kcm] of Central African Republic and Sudan.'

sources.citation: Bombay, Elaine. 2010. Enquête sociolinguistique sur les parlers Bayo, Morbo, Morom, and Bolong du Tchad: rapport. SIL Electronic Survey Reports 2010-019. Dallas: SIL International. 38 pp. (Glottolog ref 164329; the only reference Glottolog lists for gula1269; Bayo tagged [glu])
sources.note: Nothing. Sociolinguistic survey of the Guéra (Dec 2002): geography, language situation, methods, lexical similarity, intelligibility, attitudes. Sec. 4.2.2 (p. 8) describes only a 160-item wordlist collection for lexical-similarity counting ('Les différences grammaticales n'ont pas été prises en compte'). Annexe D (pp. 28-36) gives the 160-item wordlists for Kenga, Naba, Morbo, Bolongue, Bayo, Morom in broad IPA with no tone or stress marks. 'accent' occurs only in the group questionnaire (Annexe A, items 1.10-1.11) meaning regional accent. sil.org PDF is behind an automated-access block

sources.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal, Pierre Nougayrol & Pierre Palayer. 2006. Lexique comparatif historique des langues Sara-Bongo-Baguirmiennes (electronic), CNRS-LLACAN, index pagehttps://llacan.cnrs.fr/SBB/;and Boyeldieu 2006 'Présentation des langues SBB' (held)
sources.note: The Gula doculects in the SBB comparative lexicon are gula koto, gula zura, gula mere, gula sara, all sourced to Nougayrol 1999 (CAR Gula, gula1266); no Chad Gula/Bayo doculect. The presentation discusses tonal correspondences only; no word-stress statement for any Gula.

sources.citation: Glottolog 5.3, languoid gula1269 'Gula (Chad)' (Hammarström et al.),https://glottolog.org/resource/languoid/id/gula1269;plus reference pages 92825 and 164329 and languoid pages gula1266, bayo1257
sources.note: No descriptive reference at all: only Bombay 2010 (overview/wordlist/socling) and Ethnologue 2025. Alternative names Goula, Sara Gula, 'Gula (Gele)' (Ruhlen 1987), 'Gula (in Central African Republic)' (WALS). Reference 92825 (Nougayrol 1999, Les parlers gula, grammar, 382 pp.) is linked only to gula1266 [kcm]; reference 164329 (Bombay 2010) is linked to Kenga, Naba, Morbo, Bolongue, Bayo [glu], Morom.

sources.note: The only grammar of any Sara-Bongo-Bagirmi 'Gula'; has a phonology with 3-4 tone registers (per fr-Wikipedia summary) and its title covers Chad. Glottolog assigns it to gula1266 [kcm], but Ethnologue's glu is called 'Sara Gula', the same name as Nougayrol's 'gula sara' variety, so it must be opened to settle whether it describes glu at all and what it says about accent.
